Opens mid-word (τες ἐμακάριζον) completing ch. 62; English begins 'altogether fortunate' consistently.

findings.quote: they do not dare to face us head-on
findings.problem: Greek: ὅτι μόνον οὐ τολμῶσι κατὰ πρόσωπον ἰδεῖν ἡμᾶς. μόνον οὐ means 'all but / very nearly', so the Carthaginians all but do not dare; the English states it flatly and drops the hedge.
findings.proposed_fix: they all but do not dare to face us head-on
